items.stem: What is meant by “genetic engineering”?
items.answer: The technique of altering the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), introducing it into host organisms and changing their phenotype.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the technique of altering the chemistry of genetic material (DNA and RNA), introducing it into host organisms and changing their phenotype.

items.stem: In the name of the restriction enzyme EcoRI, what does "R" stand for?
items.answer: the strain RY13
items.markingKey: (c) In EcoRI, E = Escherichia, co = coli, R = strain RY13, I = first enzyme isolated from it; here: the strain RY13.
options: the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain

items.stem:

Reason (R): DNA ligase cuts DNA at specific sites.

items.answer: A is true, but R is false.
items.markingKey: (c) A is true. R is false: Restriction enzymes cut DNA; ligase joins the fragments.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “A plasmid is chromosomal DNA of bacteria.”
items.answer: A plasmid is extra-chromosomal and replicates autonomously.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: A plasmid is extra-chromosomal and replicates autonomously.

items.stem: Which of the following shows the correct basic steps in creating a genetically modified organism?
items.answer: identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny
items.markingKey: (a) identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny. These are the three basic steps.
options: identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny
introduce the identified DNA into the host → identify DNA with desirable genes → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny
maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny → identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host
identify DNA with desirable genes → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny → introduce the identified DNA into the host

items.stem:
In 1972 Cohen and Boyer cut a piece of DNA carrying an antibiotic resistance gene from a plasmid of Salmonella typhimurium and joined it to a plasmid of E. coli.
(i) Which enzyme was used to cut the DNA? (1 mark)
(ii) Which enzyme joined the cut DNA to the plasmid? (1 mark)
(iii) Why was the plasmid needed, and what happened when it was transferred to E. coli? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) A restriction enzyme (molecular scissors). (ii) DNA ligase. (iii) The plasmid acts as a vector with an origin of replication; in E. coli it replicated, making many copies of the antibiotic resistance gene (cloning).

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct basic steps in creating a genetically modified organism: identify DNA with desirable genes, maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny, introduce the identified DNA into the host. Give a reason.
items.answer: identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny; 1 mark for the reason: These are the three basic steps.

items.stem: Name the two core techniques that enabled the birth of modern biotechnology and state what each involves.
items.answer: (i) Genetic engineering – techniques to alter the chemistry of genetic material and introduce it into host organisms. (ii) Bioprocess engineering – maintenance of sterile (microbial contamination-free) conditions to enable growth of only the desired microbe or eukaryotic cell in large quantities.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each.

items.stem: Which term describes DNA formed by joining a piece of foreign DNA to a vector DNA?
items.answer: recombinant DNA
items.markingKey: (a) Recombinant DNA: DNA formed by joining a piece of foreign DNA to a vector DNA.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about principles of biotechnology and recombinant DNA is correct?
items.answer: The antibiotic resistance gene from Salmonella typhimurium was linked to a native plasmid of E. coli in the first rDNA experiment.
items.markingKey: (d) The antibiotic resistance gene from Salmonella typhimurium was linked to a native plasmid of E. coli in the first rDNA experiment. The other statements are false. It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model. A plasmid is extra-chromosomal and replicates autonomously. Restriction enzymes cut DNA; ligase joins the fragments.
options: DNA ligase cuts DNA at specific sites.
The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.
A plasmid is chromosomal DNA of bacteria.
The antibiotic resistance gene from Salmonella typhimurium was linked to a native plasmid of E. coli in the first rDNA experiment.

items.stem: Which of the following sequences (5′ → 3′ on one strand) is a palindrome that could be a restriction enzyme recognition site?
items.answer: 5′-AGTACT-3′
items.markingKey: (a) 5′-AGTACT-3′ is a palindrome: its complementary strand, read 5′ → 3′, is also AGTACT. The other sequences do not read the same on both strands.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.
Reason (R): Biotechnology deals with large-scale production and marketing of products using live organisms or their enzymes.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “a plasmid”.
items.answer: An autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA in bacteria.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: an autonomously replicating circular extra-chromosomal DNA in bacteria.

items.stem: Why is it necessary to link a foreign DNA to an origin of replication for it to be cloned?
items.answer: The ori is the sequence from where replication starts; a piece of DNA that is linked to the ori can replicate within the host cell. Without it, the foreign DNA cannot multiply in the host and is not cloned.
items.markingKey: 1 mark role of ori; 1 mark consequence.

items.stem: Explain the term “insertional inactivation”.
items.answer: The inactivation of a gene in a vector when foreign DNA is inserted into it, used to identify recombinants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the inactivation of a gene in a vector when foreign DNA is inserted into it, used to identify recombinants.

items.stem: Classify each of the following as feature of a cloning vector or tool for introducing DNA into a host: origin of replication, biolistics (gene gun), heat shock with Ca²⁺, selectable marker.
items.answer: origin of replication – feature of a cloning vector; biolistics (gene gun) – tool for introducing DNA into a host; heat shock with Ca²⁺ – tool for introducing DNA into a host; selectable marker – feature of a cloning vector.
items.markingKey: ½ mark each: origin of replication – feature of a cloning vector; biolistics (gene gun) – tool for introducing DNA into a host; heat shock with Ca²⁺ – tool for introducing DNA into a host; selectable marker – feature of a cloning vector.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): DNA can pass through the cell membrane of bacteria without any treatment.
Reason (R): More than 900 restriction enzymes have been isolated from over 230 strains of bacteria.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: DNA is hydrophilic; cells must be made competent, e.g. with Ca²⁺ and heat shock. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A part of the plasmid vector pBR322 has this role: present once in the vector; sequence where replication starts. Identify the part.
items.answer: ori

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Blue-white selection is preferred over antibiotic replica plating.
Reason (R): It needs only a single plating on a chromogenic substrate.

items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Replica plating on two antibiotics is cumbersome.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem:
Kavya cuts a 10 kb linear DNA with EcoRI, which has three recognition sites in it, and also cuts a plasmid with one EcoRI site.
(i) How many fragments does she get from the linear DNA and from the plasmid? (1 mark)
(ii) What is the recognition sequence of EcoRI? (1 mark)
(iii) Why are sticky ends formed, and why must the same enzyme cut both DNAs? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Four fragments from the linear DNA; the plasmid opens into one linear piece. (ii) 5′-GAATTC-3′ (cuts between G and A). (iii) EcoRI cuts a little away from the centre of the palindrome on both strands, leaving single-stranded overhangs; the same enzyme gives complementary sticky ends that can pair and be joined by DNA ligase.

items.stem: How is a bacterial cell made competent to take up recombinant DNA?
items.answer: The cells are treated with a specific concentration of a divalent cation such as calcium, which increases the efficiency of DNA entry through pores in the cell wall; they are then incubated with the rDNA on ice, given a brief heat shock at 42 °C, and put back on ice.
items.markingKey: 1 mark Ca²⁺; 1 mark heat shock.

items.stem: Which of the following is a restriction endonuclease?
items.answer: EcoRI
items.markingKey: (b) EcoRI is a restriction endonuclease; the others are not.

items.stem: Which of the following is a restriction endonuclease?
items.answer: SalI
items.markingKey: (b) SalI is a restriction endonuclease; the others are not.

items.answer: insertional inactivation
items.markingKey: (a) Insertional inactivation: the inactivation of a gene in a vector when foreign DNA is inserted into it, used to identify recombinants.

items.stem: What is the role of the ori site in recombinant DNA technology?
items.answer: starts replication and controls the copy number of the plasmid
items.markingKey: (d) The ori site: starts replication and controls the copy number of the plasmid (any DNA linked to it can replicate).
options: synthesises DNA at high temperature during PCR
removes nucleotides from the ends of DNA
breaks the bacterial cell wall to release DNA
starts replication and controls the copy number of the plasmid

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a tool for introducing DNA into a host?

items.stem: Which tool or component of rDNA technology helps identify and eliminate non-transformants?

items.stem:
A biotechnology firm in Hyderabad grows recombinant E. coli in a 1000-litre stirred-tank bioreactor to make a protein drug.
(i) Why is a stirred-tank bioreactor used instead of shake flasks? (1 mark)
(ii) Name any two conditions the bioreactor must keep optimal. (1 mark)
(iii) What is downstream processing and why is quality control essential here? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) For large volumes (100–1000 L) with even mixing and better oxygen availability. (ii) Temperature, pH, substrate, salts, vitamins, oxygen (any two). (iii) Separation and purification of the product, and formulation with preservatives; a drug must pass strict quality control and clinical trials for safety.

items.stem:

(b) A part of a stirred-tank bioreactor has this function: adds antifoam when needed. Identify the part – the foam control system or the sparger? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) The foam control system: prevents foaming; adds antifoam when needed; at the top of the vessel. The sparger: bubbles sterile air into the medium; improves oxygen transfer; near the base. (b) The foam control system.

items.stem: Describe how DNA fragments are separated and visualised by gel electrophoresis.
items.answer: DNA fragments are loaded into wells of an agarose gel and an electric field is applied; being negatively charged they move towards the anode, smaller fragments moving farther through the sieve-like matrix. The gel is stained with ethidium bromide and exposed to UV light: DNA appears as bright orange bands, which can be cut out and eluted.
items.markingKey: 1 mark separation; 1 mark visualisation.

items.stem: Give two differences between the sparger and the agitator (stirrer).

items.markingKey: 1 mark for each correct, paired difference, e.g. the sparger – part of the aeration system; near the base; the agitator (stirrer) – mixes the contents; keeps cells in suspension.

items.stem: Explain the steps of the polymerase chain reaction with a diagram. Why is Taq polymerase used?
items.answer: PCR amplifies a gene in vitro. (i) Denaturation: double-stranded DNA is heated (~94 °C) to separate strands. (ii) Annealing: two sets of primers bind to complementary regions at a lower temperature. (iii) Extension: Taq polymerase extends the primers using dNTPs, copying the region between them. Repeated cycles amplify the DNA about a billion times (2ⁿ copies). Taq polymerase from Thermus aquaticus is thermostable and remains active through the high temperature of denaturation.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each step (3); 1 mark diagram; 1 mark Taq.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about principles of biotechnology and recombinant DNA is incorrect?
items.answer: The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.
items.markingKey: (c) The incorrect statement is “The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.” Correct form: It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model.
options: Restriction enzymes and DNA ligase are the basic tools of rDNA technology.
The first recombinant DNA was made by Stanley Cohen and Herbert Boyer in 1972.
The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.
The antibiotic resistance gene from Salmonella typhimurium was linked to a native plasmid of E. coli in the first rDNA experiment.

items.stem: Which enzyme is used to break open plant cells to isolate DNA?
items.answer: cellulase
items.markingKey: (c) Lysozyme for bacteria, cellulase for plant cells, chitinase for fungi: cellulase.

items.stem: Which term describes an enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific position within it after recognising a specific palindromic sequence?
items.answer: a restriction endonuclease
items.markingKey: (b) A restriction endonuclease: an enzyme that cuts DNA at a specific position within it after recognising a specific palindromic sequence.

items.stem: A part of a stirred-tank bioreactor has this function: motor driven; keeps cells in suspension; mixes the contents. Identify the part. Give a reason.
items.answer: The agitator (stirrer)
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the agitator (stirrer); 1 mark: the features motor driven; keeps cells in suspension; mixes the contents are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a cloning vector?
items.answer: EcoRI
items.markingKey: (d) EcoRI is a restriction endonuclease, not a feature of a cloning vector.

items.stem: A restriction enzyme recognises a specific 6-bp palindromic sequence. Assuming all four bases occur equally and randomly, how many times would this site be expected to occur in a DNA of 10000 bp?
items.answer: about 2.4 times
items.markingKey: Probability of a given 6-bp sequence = (1/4)^6 = 1/4096 (1); expected sites = 10000 / 4096 ≈ 2.4 (1).

items.stem: Starting with one DNA molecule, how many PCR cycles are needed to obtain 64 copies (100% efficiency)?
items.answer: 6 cycles
items.markingKey: (a) Copies = 2ⁿ; 2^6 = 64, so n = 6.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Smaller DNA fragments move slower in agarose gel.
Reason (R): Most commonly used bioreactors are of the stirring type.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: Smaller fragments move farther; the matrix acts as a sieve. R is a true statement.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Define the term “a selectable marker”.
items.answer: A gene that helps in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of transformants.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a gene that helps in identifying and eliminating non-transformants and selectively permitting the growth of transformants.

items.stem:
Assertion (A): Restriction enzymes are called molecular scissors.
Reason (R): They cut DNA at specific recognition sequences.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) They cut at specific sites.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: A circular plasmid has 3 recognition sites for BamHI. How many DNA fragments are obtained on complete digestion with BamHI?
items.markingKey: (a) A circular molecule cut at 3 site(s) gives 3 fragment(s), as there are no free ends.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct basic steps in creating a genetically modified organism: maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny, identify DNA with desirable genes, introduce the identified DNA into the host. Give a reason.
items.answer: identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order identify DNA with desirable genes → introduce the identified DNA into the host → maintain the introduced DNA in the host and transfer to progeny; 1 mark for the reason: These are the three basic steps.

items.stem: A part of a stirred-tank bioreactor has this function: motor driven; distributes oxygen evenly. Identify the part.
items.answer: the agitator (stirrer)
items.markingKey: (c) The agitator (stirrer): motor driven; distributes oxygen evenly.

items.stem: In the name of the restriction enzyme EcoRI, what does "I" stand for?
items.answer: the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain
items.markingKey: (a) In EcoRI, E = Escherichia, co = coli, R = strain RY13, I = first enzyme isolated from it; here: the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain.
options: the order in which the enzyme was isolated from that strain

items.stem: Which term describes a large vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products under optimal conditions?
items.answer: a bioreactor
items.markingKey: (c) A bioreactor: a large vessel in which raw materials are biologically converted into specific products under optimal conditions.

items.stem: A foreign gene is ligated into the SalI site of pBR322, which lies in the tetracycline resistance gene. On which media will E. coli cells carrying the recombinant plasmid grow?
items.answer: grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline
items.markingKey: (c) Insertion at SalI inactivates the tetracycline resistance gene (insertional inactivation); the ampicillin resistance gene is still intact.
options: grow on tetracycline but not on ampicillin
grow on ampicillin but not on tetracycline

items.stem: Which of the following statements about principles of biotechnology and recombinant DNA is correct?
items.answer: Biotechnology deals with large-scale production and marketing of products using live organisms or their enzymes.
items.markingKey: (c) Biotechnology deals with large-scale production and marketing of products using live organisms or their enzymes. The other statements are false. It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model. A plasmid is extra-chromosomal and replicates autonomously. Restriction enzymes cut DNA; ligase joins the fragments.
options: DNA ligase cuts DNA at specific sites.
A plasmid is chromosomal DNA of bacteria.
Biotechnology deals with large-scale production and marketing of products using live organisms or their enzymes.
The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.

items.stem: Arrange the following in the correct sequence of steps in rDNA technology: culturing the host and extraction of the product, fragmentation by restriction endonuclease, ligation into a vector, isolation of DNA. Give a reason.
items.answer: isolation of DNA → fragmentation by restriction endonuclease → ligation into a vector → culturing the host and extraction of the product
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the order isolation of DNA → fragmentation by restriction endonuclease → ligation into a vector → culturing the host and extraction of the product; 1 mark for the reason: As described in NCERT.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about tools of rDNA technology is incorrect?
items.answer: DNA can pass through the cell membrane of bacteria without any treatment.
items.markingKey: (b) The incorrect statement is “DNA can pass through the cell membrane of bacteria without any treatment.” Correct form: DNA is hydrophilic; cells must be made competent, e.g. with Ca²⁺ and heat shock.
options: Retroviruses are disarmed before being used as vectors in animal cells.
DNA can pass through the cell membrane of bacteria without any treatment.
Agrobacterium tumefaciens delivers DNA into dicot plants by its Ti plasmid.
The first restriction endonuclease to be isolated was HindII.

items.stem: The following statement is incorrect. Rewrite it correctly and give a reason: “The first recombinant DNA was made in 1953.”
items.answer: It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: It was made in 1972 by Cohen and Boyer; 1953 is the year of the Watson–Crick model.
